html:
The Sudanese civil war began on 15 April 2023, when the Sudanese army under General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan and the Rapid Support Forces under General Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as Hemedti, turned on each other in Khartoum.

The two had led the coup of 2021 together but fell out over merging the RSF, which grew out of the Janjaweed militias of the Darfur war, into the army. Fighting wrecked Khartoum, and the RSF was accused of ethnic massacres in Darfur.

Over ten million people were driven from their homes, the largest displacement crisis in the world, and famine was confirmed in parts of the country in 2024. Foreign powers backed each side. The war divided Sudan, with the army holding the east and the RSF much of the west.
